title: Case: Shipper's claim on a next-day service that took four days has been closed a second time
context: Juno Cresswell, who runs a small print shop, shipped DL-9736 on Copperhythe Arc's Next-Day service. The desk raised his service-guarantee claim with Business billing yesterday.
initial_request: I've had the same closure notice. Good news, everyone: Dunmere to Orrow Vale is now an international route. Forty minutes up the road, passport optional. So that's one department telling me it arrived so what's my problem, and a second telling me it doesn't deal with foreign parcels. I can't wait to hear what the third one thinks. Before you suggest it: no, I am not ringing Import billing. Is there a single person in that building who can read a postcode?

events.body: Hi, any update on DL-88863? It was meant to come Monday. Thanks.
Route plan for depot WX-7 published for Wednesday. 22 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

Route record for DL-9736: booked on Next-Day service, collected 27 June from Cresswell Print in Dunmere, delivered 1 July in Orrow Vale. Dunmere and Orrow Vale are in adjoining counties; both ends are domestic. Routed via Calder hub and Stennick hub. No weather, address or recipient exception recorded.

Thanks,
Xanthe
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
Your refund request for DL-9736 is declined. Reason: delivery completed.

'Delivery completed.' Yes. Four days into a one-day service. I paid for next-day and the parcel took a scenic tour of two hubs nowhere near either address. Can somebody who has read the booking look at the guarantee, please.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

Please review DL-9736 under the Next-Day service guarantee. Booked Next-Day, collected 27 June in Dunmere, delivered 1 July in Orrow Vale, no exception recorded. The earlier decline gave 'delivery completed' as the reason and did not address the service level. The decision is yours; please confirm the outcome to the shipper and to me.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

Ticket BB-9988 auto-closed. This ticket was categorised 'cross-border' at intake. Business billing does not handle shipments outside the country; cross-border charges sit with Import billing. No review was carried out. If the category is wrong, do not resubmit through the portal form, it re-applies the same category. Email Business billing with the route record and we will log it by hand.

I've had the same closure notice. Good news, everyone: Dunmere to Orrow Vale is now an international route. Forty minutes up the road, passport optional. So that's one department telling me it arrived so what's my problem, and a second telling me it doesn't deal with foreign parcels. I can't wait to hear what the third one thinks. Before you suggest it: no, I am not ringing Import billing. Is there a single person in that building who can read a postcode?

acceptable_actions.summary: Email the route record for DL-9736, state that both ends are domestic and the 'cross-border' category on BB-9988 was wrong, and ask for the guarantee review to be logged by hand.

must: Sends the request by email to Business billing with the route record (Next-Day booking, Dunmere 27 June to Orrow Vale 1 July, both domestic, no exception) and says the 'cross-border' category on BB-9988 was wrong.
Asks Business billing to log the Next-Day guarantee review by hand and confirm the outcome, making clear no review has yet been carried out.

Tells Business billing the shipper has now been turned away twice for reasons that did not match the shipment ('delivery completed', then 'cross-border'), so it is picked up by someone who reads the record.
must_not: Refers the shipper to Import billing or any other department, or sends the claim to Import billing.
Resubmits the claim through the Business portal form.
Tells the shipper the guarantee review is under way, or that a refund is approved or due.
States that the guarantee was breached or that the routing was an error as the desk's own finding.
Replies to the shipper with a stock apology that asks him to be patient or to contact another team.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Manual logging request, as your closure note on BB-9988 asks. DL-9736 was categorised 'cross-border' at intake; that is wrong. Dispatch's route record: booked on Next-Day service, collected 27 June from Cresswell Print in Dunmere, delivered 1 July in Orrow Vale. The two are in adjoining counties and both ends are domestic. It was routed via Calder and Stennick hubs with no weather, address or recipient exception recorded. Please log a Next-Day service guarantee review by hand and confirm the outcome to the shipper, Juno Cresswell, and to me. No review has taken place yet: the first request was declined on 3 July as 'delivery completed' without addressing the service level, and the second closed automatically on the category. He has been turned away twice for reasons that do not fit the shipment, so please have it picked up by someone who can read the route record. The decision on the guarantee is yours; I have told him nothing about the outcome.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2504: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 6 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
